requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:76-84 appends "\n<@id>" after the content and reserves room via `self::MaxContentLength - mb_strlen($suffix)`, so a truncated alert is still 1800 chars and keeps the mention; the no-mention path at :72-73 is the original `mb_substr($base, 0, self::MaxContentLength)`. mentionId() (:87-106) accepts int or string, trims, and requires `/^[0-9]{17,20}$/`, so @everyone, @here, abc, 123 and the embedded-newline values are rejected (trim only strips the ends, so "123\n@everyone" fails the regex). Config key `services.discord.mention_id` <- `DISCORD_MENTION_ID` (config/services.php:40), and the .env.example and both ops docs are updated. send() and the webhook/redaction paths are untouched.

conventions.evidence: No Pest/PHPUnit test in the diff, which breaks the 'No production code without a test' TDD rule. CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] is not updated, although the conventions require it. Docs are kept in sync in docs/ops/devops.md:61,70 and docs/ops/logging.md:83, and the private helper style matches the sibling `safe()` method.

security.evidence: The strict snowflake allow-list `preg_match('/^[0-9]{17,20}$/', $value)` after trim() blocks mass-mention and injection values. Redaction (`$this->safe(...)`) and URL-free failure logging are unchanged. No user input, Livewire or authorization surface is involved.

tests.evidence: change.diff touches no files under tests/. Nothing tests the mention suffix, the invalid-ID rejections, the truncation that keeps the mention, or that the no-mention behaviour is unchanged.

simplicity.evidence: The change is short and direct. It has small redundancies: `$value === ''` is already covered by the regex, the `$available < 0` clamp can never trigger (the suffix is at most 24 chars), and `$mention` is only used to build `$suffix`.

readability.evidence: Names are clear (`mentionId()`, `$suffix`, `$available`) and the early return for the no-mention path is easy to follow. No PHPDoc explains the snowflake rule on mentionId().

scope.evidence: Every hunk serves the task: the class, config/services.php, .env.example and the two ops docs. The only incidental edit is the removed blank line in .env.example:78.

issues.explanation: The new behaviour ships with no test, which violates the project's mandatory TDD rule: no test covers valid/invalid mention IDs, mention placement, or the 1800-char truncation that keeps the mention.
The conventions require a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased], but none was added for the new DISCORD_MENTION_ID feature.
The `$available < 0` clamp can never trigger and the `$value === ''` check is already covered by the regex, so both are dead code.
The blank line separating the Discord block from the Hostinger block was removed, so the two sections now run together.

review.summary: The change adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID setting and appends a strictly validated `<@snowflake>` mention on its own line. It reserves room for the mention under the 1800-char limit and documents the variable in .env.example and the ops docs. The implementation is correct and secure, but there are no tests, which the project's TDD conventions require, and no CHANGELOG entry, so it needs changes before merging.
